thread:
samira-sales: Hey team — Acme POC ran into a blocker when we flipped them to Private (VPC). App logs show `tls: handshake failure` and our side shows connection resets. They say DNS + certs are configured on their side. Can we triage?
ryan-eng: What endpoint are they hitting? public or private endpoint?
samira-sales: Private endpoint: `private.acme.redwood-internal.svc`. They created a CNAME from their internal DNS to our private endpoint IP.
mia-netops: Can you paste the curl/openssl output from their client? Also need the dig results for their internal name.
jake-support: Pasted from their support ticket: `curl -v https://private.acme.redwood-internal.svc/` ->
```
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 10.240.12.45 port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert handshake failure
```
ryan-eng: That looks like an SNI/cert mismatch or cipher issue. Ask them to run `openssl s_client -connect 10.240.12.45:443 -servername private.acme.redwood-internal.svc -showcerts` and paste the cert chain.
samira-sales: They ran it; here's what they got (trimmed):
```
subject=CN = internal.redwood.local
issuer=CN = Redwood Dev CA
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: DNS:private.redwood.internal, DNS:localhost
```
mia-netops: Aha — cert CN/SAN doesn't include their internal name `private.acme.redwood-internal.svc`. SNI -> cert mismatch will cause handshake failure if client enforces hostname check.
anna-security: Also confirm firewall: they must allow outbound to our private endpoint IP on 443 from their app subnet. Any packet drops in flow logs?
jake-support: Customer provided VPC flow logs — we see `REJECT` entries for TCP dst port 443 from their app subnet to 10.240.12.45 around the same timestamps.
mia-netops: So two simultaneous issues: (1) firewall/NACL blocking, (2) cert SANS mismatch. Firewall is easy — they need an allow rule for destination 10.240.12.45/32 on TCP/443 (or 10.240.12.0/24 if using autoscaling).
ryan-eng: For the cert: options are — have them add the private name to the SANs on their internal DNS or (preferred) create a CNAME that matches a SAN we already present, or use our private TLS provisioning so we emit a cert with the expected SAN. Which POC option are they on?
samira-sales: They're on self-managed DNS but asked us to accept their cert. They uploaded a cert but probably with wrong SANs.
anna-security: If they upload their own cert, it must include the VPC-private hostname in SAN. Also confirm the cert chain includes an issuer we trust; we allow private CA chains only if admin config enabled for Private deployments.
jake-support: Quick remediation steps sent to customer: 1) Add firewall rule allow to 10.240.12.45:443 2) Re-issue cert with SAN `private.acme.redwood-internal.svc` or set CNAME to one of our SAN'd hostnames 3) Test with `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername <hostname>` 4) Share output.
samira-sales: Customer tried adding rule but still failing — they reported `certificate verify failed: certificate has expired`. Their chain shows a leaf expiry in 2021.
mia-netops: OK expired cert — they replaced it now?
samira-sales: They rotated cert and now `openssl s_client` returns OK but app still sees `connection reset`.
ryan-eng: Check MTU/path or ALB health? If handshake completes but connection reset after, could be backend closing due to missing Host header or mTLS expectation. Any 495/496 style codes in our ingress?
devops-bot: Canary release to private-stack completed (version 2026.3.4). No errors reported.
jake-support: Our ingress logs show `400 Bad Request` for Host mismatch for that session. The client used host `private.acme.redwood-internal.svc` but our router expects `private.acme.redwood.internal` (dot vs dash). Could be DNS alias confusion.
samira-sales: Their internal DNS had a hyphen vs dot mistake — they fixed it now. After fix, QA reports success and tokens flowing.
anna-security: Filing note for the security questionnaire: POC showed we require either customer-managed cert with correct SANs or alternative of Redwood-managed cert (opt-in). Document both options under 'networking blockers' FAQ.
ryan-eng: TL;DR for AE: 1) Check VPC flow logs for REJECT 2) Verify cert SAN matches requested hostname (use `openssl s_client -servername`) 3) Confirm Host header & DNS alias match exactly 4) If still failing, paste `curl -v` and ingress logs.
samira-sales: Thanks all — I'm updating the deal ticket and sending the remediation steps. :thumbsup:
